general_theorem.name: SIGNED_LITERAL_SUBSTITUTION_MODEL_TRANSPORT
general_theorem.setup: Let A be a target CNF and B a source CNF. Let phi map every variable of A to a signed literal over variables of B, with repetitions allowed and phi(-v)=-phi(v). For every target clause C require either phi(C) is tautological, or there exists a source clause D in B with D subseteq phi(C).
general_theorem.assignment_transport: For every source assignment alpha define beta(v) as the truth value of the signed source literal phi(v) under alpha.
general_theorem.conclusion: alpha models B implies beta models A. Therefore SAT(B) implies SAT(A), so in a sibling OR state the source sibling B can be deleted when A is retained.
proof: Fix alpha satisfying B and target clause C.
If phi(C) is tautological, beta satisfies C automatically.
Otherwise choose D in B with D subseteq phi(C). Since alpha satisfies D, alpha satisfies phi(C).
By the definition of beta, beta satisfies C iff alpha satisfies phi(C).
Thus beta satisfies every target clause.
general_theorem.verification_cost: Given phi and one clause/tautology witness per target clause, verification is polynomial in the encoded formulas.
general_theorem.strict_generalization: Signed permutation transport is the special case where phi is a bijection on underlying variables.

critical_instance.model_replay: All seven source-B models map to satisfying assignments of A.
critical_instance.safe_deletion: SAT(B) implies SAT(A), hence SAT(A) OR SAT(B) iff SAT(A). Delete B and retain A.

strictness_certificate.R44BR_fact: All 5!*2^5 signed permutations fail in both directions.
strictness_certificate.R44BS_fact: The displayed many-to-one substitution succeeds B->A.
strictness_certificate.conclusion: MANY_TO_ONE_SUBSTITUTION_TRANSPORT strictly extends the effective safe-deletion power of SIGNED_PERMUTATION_TRANSPORT on an exact maxdef-critical sibling instance.

next_exact_question: Can the many-to-one signed literal substitution class be discovered in polynomial time on a nontrivial critical family, or is generic/critical discovery hard? If generic discovery is hard, isolate a polynomially discoverable subclass that still strictly exceeds R44BP and test universal critical coverage with exact counterexamples.
